Topic.label: Linear Functions and Linear Equations in One Variable

Question: How is the \(x\)-coordinate of the intersection of the graph of the linear function \(y=2x-6\) with the \(x\)-axis related to the solution of \(2x-6=0\)?
Solution: Points on the \(x\)-axis have \(y\)-coordinate \(y=0\). Substituting this into \(y=2x-6\) gives \(2x-6=0\), so the \(x\)-coordinate of the intersection is the solution of the equation. Solving gives \(x=3\).
